Issued at 250 PM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

Currently-Tonight...Showers and storms have been developing near 
to south of a line from Orlando to Melbourne along the east coast 
sea breeze and a differential heating boundary created from debris
cloud cover over northern portions of east central FL. Showers 
and storms will continue to increase, especially from near the 
Orlando metro area southward through Osceola, Okeechobee counties 
and the Treasure Coast from outflow collisions and the advancing 
east coast sea breeze. 10Z sounding at the Cape this morning 
showed a very saturated airmass, with a PW value of 2.5" (a record
for the day based off SPC sounding climatology), as well as warm 
temps aloft (around -4C at 500mb). DCAPE also remains rather low 
(around 400-500 J/kg) on SPC Mesoscale Analysis. Therefore threat 
for any stronger wind gusts remains low, but gusts up to 30 to 40 
mph and occasional to frequent lightning will still occur. The 
deep tropical moisture in place will keep locally heavy to 
excessive rainfall the main threat from storms or heavier showers 
today. Quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3 inches will be very 
easy to occur from any storms through this afternoon/evening, 
leading to mostly minor flooding of roadways and poor drainage 
areas. However, there remains a low (5-10% chance) for totals of 
4+ inches, which may lead to isolated instances of flash flooding.
A Marginal Risk for Excessive Rainfall (Level 1 of 4) remains in 
place across east central Florida for today. 

Convection should begin to diminish past sunset with the loss of 
daytime heating, but a few storms with lingering areas of debris 
cloud cover rainfall may persist through the evening hours. Drier 
conditions expected overnight, with low level flow becoming more 
southerly, which should keep most convection that develops over the 
waters offshore. Warm and very muggy overnight, with lows in the mid 
to upper 70s for most locations. 

Friday-Saturday...PW values forecast to actually decrease some, but 
still remain high around 2.0-2.2" through late week and into early 
weekend, as ridge axis of high pressure across the west Atlantic 
settles southward across the area. With the continued moist airmass 
in place and weak steering flow, locally heavy rainfall around 2-4" 
and mostly minor flooding will continue to be a threat from slow 
moving or persistent storms and heavier showers. The Weather 
Prediction Center maintains a Marginal (level 1 of 4) Risk for 
excessive rainfall through at least Friday. Scattered to numerous 
showers and storms will develop each day, with increasing coverage 
from late morning into the afternoon. Low level flow will become 
more southerly Friday, with boundary collisions favored well
inland. Flow then turns south-southwesterly Saturday, shifting 
the sea breeze collision a little farther east across east central
Florida. Rain chances range from 50-70 percent, with highest
chances across the interior tomorrow and 70 percent areawide on
Saturday. Temperatures increase a tad, but still near to just 
slightly above normal, with highs in the low 90s and some mid 90s 
possible across the interior. Peak heat index values will reach 
100-107F ahead of any storms. Overnight conditions will remain
warm and humid with lows in the 70s.

Sunday-Wednesday...(Previous Discussion) The trough over the eastern 
seaboard and western Atlantic is forecast to reach just offshore the 
Southeast seaboard Sunday or so, ushering a weakening front into the 
Deep South, and possibly reaching Florida Monday or Tuesday. There 
remains some uncertainty how far south the boundary will make it, 
and more uncertainty where weak disturbances may develop on the 
boundary as it stalls. Both impact whether East Central Florida 
remains in the subtropical soup or if some drier air will finally 
reach the area, what kinda of support there is for convection, and 
what flow regime we end up in. Given the uncertainty the official 
forecast trends towards the ensembles and blends, which call for 
broad stroked rain chances to remain above normal, but do decrease a 
bit towards mid-next week. Seasonable temperatures stay on the 
hotter side through the weekend, then tick down a degree or two for 
the work week.
